changes.location: Executive Summary › paragraph 1
changes.before: Irontrax’s Q3 assessment continues the findings and historical context reported in Q1 and Q2, using the current Microsoft Secure Score indicators and recommended-action statuses as the observable baseline. The review covers Microsoft-reported identity, data, email, and collaboration controls. Endpoint, vulnerability, cloud workload, AI, and incident-response evidence were not available, so those domains remain unassessed rather than being presumed secure or unchanged.
changes.after: Irontrax’s Q3 assessment extends the findings and historical context reported in Q1 and Q2. It uses the current Microsoft Secure Score indicators and recommended-action statuses as the observable baseline, covering Microsoft-reported identity, data, email, and collaboration controls. Endpoint, vulnerability, cloud workload, AI, and incident-response evidence were not available, so those domains remain unassessed rather than presumed secure or unchanged.
changes.reason: Separates the scope statement from the baseline description so the paragraph states its scope before the evidence limits.

changes.location: Executive Summary › paragraph 2
changes.before: Microsoft Secure Score is 39.33%, with 105 of 267 available points, compared with 38.6% and 105 of 272 points in both prior assessments. The 0.73 percentage-point increase reflects a smaller available-point denominator, not additional earned points or demonstrated remediation. Identity remains the strongest scored category at 96.72%; Data remains at 0% and Apps at 23.35%. These indicators help prioritize configuration review but do not establish overall risk maturity or framework compliance.
changes.after: The Q3 Microsoft Secure Score is 39.33%, with 105 of 267 available points, compared with 38.6% (105 of 272 points) in both prior assessments. The 0.73 percentage-point increase results from a smaller available-point denominator. It reflects no additional earned points and no demonstrated remediation. Identity remains the strongest scored category at 96.72%, while Data remains at 0% and Apps at 23.35%. These indicators help prioritize configuration review. They do not establish overall risk maturity or framework compliance.
changes.reason: Leads with the supported score conclusion and states the movement as a denominator effect with no earned change, one claim per sentence.

changes.location: Executive Summary › paragraph 3
changes.before: The primary Q3 concern is the continuing gap between Microsoft-reported identity protection and the less complete data and collaboration control baseline. The three recommendations first identified in 2024-Q2 remain open: restricting additional storage providers in Outlook on the web, preventing user installation of Outlook add-ins, and requiring modern authentication for SharePoint applications. Current action statuses support retaining these recommendations, but do not establish that no remediation work has occurred.
changes.after: The primary Q3 concern is the continuing gap between strong Microsoft-reported identity protection and a less complete data and collaboration control baseline. The three recommendations first identified in 2024-Q2 remain open: restricting additional storage providers in Outlook on the web, preventing user installation of Outlook add-ins, and requiring modern authentication for SharePoint applications. The current action statuses support retaining these recommendations. They do not establish that no remediation work has occurred.
changes.reason: Splits the comma-joined support and limitation into separate sentences so the retention conclusion and its qualification are each stated once.

changes.location: Executive Summary › paragraph 4
changes.before: The current review also brings attention to common attachment filtering, data loss prevention, mail forwarding restrictions, mailbox auditing, external calendar sharing, and Teams meeting controls. These are newly emphasized in this assessment, not proven to have first arisen during Q3. No prior recommendation can be confirmed resolved, and the essentially flat Q3 score trends do not support a conclusion of major gains or regressions.
changes.after: This review also emphasizes common attachment filtering, data loss prevention, mail forwarding restrictions, mailbox auditing, external calendar sharing, and Teams meeting controls. These items are newly emphasized in this assessment; the evidence does not show that they first arose in Q3. No prior recommendation can be confirmed resolved. The essentially flat Q3 score trends do not support a conclusion of major gains or regressions.
changes.reason: Makes the Q3 timing qualification explicit and separates the no-resolution finding from the trend conclusion.

changes.location: Current Microsoft Cloud Security Posture › Posture Summary
changes.before: Of 69 recommended actions, Microsoft reports 28 Completed and 41 To address. Among the open actions, 22 carry a Have license value of Yes and 19 a value of No. These flags are not independently verified entitlements: some advanced controls have inconsistent flags across completed and pending actions. Peer scores of 46.8% overall and 60.9% for identity provide comparison context only, not an assurance standard or a reliable measure of Irontrax’s risk maturity.
changes.after: Microsoft reports 28 of 69 recommended actions as Completed and 41 as To address, so most recommended actions remain open. Among the open actions, 22 carry a Have license value of Yes and 19 a value of No. These flags are not independently verified entitlements, and some advanced controls show inconsistent flags across completed and pending actions. Peer scores of 46.8% overall and 60.9% for identity provide comparison context only. They are not an assurance standard or a reliable measure of Irontrax’s risk maturity.
changes.reason: Leads with the open-action condition, then the entitlement qualification, then the peer-comparison limit.

changes.location: Current Microsoft Cloud Security Posture › Control Movement and Baseline Changes › paragraph 1
changes.before: Q1 and Q2 each reported 38.6% overall (105/272), 89.39% Identity, 0% Data, and 23.35% Apps. Q3 reports 39.33% overall (105/267), 96.72% Identity, 0% Data, and 23.35% Apps. Identity is 7.33 percentage points higher and currently earns 59/61 points, but no comparable prior identity point breakdown or control-by-control baseline is available to attribute that increase to specific remediation. The July–September trends are essentially flat. Neither the unchanged earned total nor a flat trend establishes that no security changes occurred.
changes.after: Identity rose from 89.39% in Q1 and Q2 to 96.72% in Q3, a 7.33 percentage-point increase, and now earns 59 of 61 points. No comparable prior identity point breakdown or control-by-control baseline is available, so the increase cannot be attributed to a specific remediation. Overall scores were 38.6% (105/272) in Q1 and Q2 and 39.33% (105/267) in Q3, with Data at 0% and Apps at 23.35% in all three quarters. The July–September trends are essentially flat. Neither the unchanged earned total nor the flat trend establishes that no security changes occurred.
changes.reason: Leads with the identity movement and its attribution limit, replacing the vague 'currently' with the quarter-anchored Q3 scores.

observations.location: Recommended Security Actions › Security Awareness; Current Microsoft Cloud Security Posture › AI Agents and Generative AI Usage (closing paragraph)
observations.detail: The AI section states that the awareness guidance in this report addresses verification of impersonation attempts. The Security Awareness call-out instead addresses cloud misconfigurations and shadow APIs. The Advisory Recommendations table records Q1 emphasis on impersonation verification. The sentence does not match the awareness content. Not corrected, per the substance freeze.

observations.location: Security Signal Review › Identity and Access (Defender / Secure Score control evidence table)
observations.detail: Earned points listed in the identity control table total 58 (10 + 9 + 8 + 4 + 1 + 7 + 7 + 1 + 3 + 8), against the reported 59 of 61 identity points earned. The one-point difference is not explained by the listed rows. Not corrected, per the substance freeze.

observations.location: Executive Summary; Current Microsoft Cloud Security Posture › Domain Posture; Recommended Security Actions › Active Recommendations and CIS Microsoft 365 Foundation Benchmark
observations.detail: Quarter identifiers are written as 2024-Q2 and 2024-Q3 in prose and as 2024 Q2 in tables. The template convention is YYYY.QQ. Dates are not used consistently across sections.

observations.location: Recommended Security Actions › Active Recommendations; CIS Microsoft 365 Foundation Benchmark
observations.detail: The template requires MM.DD.YYYY - <STATUS DESCRIPTION> for each status. The draft provides no per-item dates; status values are quarter-labeled (for example, '2026 Q3: All three remain To address'). The draft value is retained.

observations.location: Current Microsoft Cloud Security Posture › Domain Posture
observations.detail: The template states that domain indicators are carried forward from the previous assessment. The draft states that Q1 and Q2 did not establish comparable domain-level indicators, so none are carried forward. The draft explanation is retained.

observations.location: Security Signal Review › Endpoint and Vulnerabilities (exposure level table)
observations.detail: The template expects numeric exposure counts (#) in each cell. The draft records 'Not available' for every quarter. The draft value is retained because no exposure data was supplied.

The template places the Security Awareness content as a heading followed by two to four paragraphs. The draft places it in a single-cell table. The content is preserved unchanged under the Security Awareness exemption, and table structure is frozen.

observations.detail: The draft contains four '[image]' placeholders for Secure Score screenshots (overview and identity). The template expects these as screenshot placeholders. Image content is not present in the markdown and must be confirmed in the final DOCX.
